$comment: Nothing outside this file may be created, written to or modified in
Microsoft Fabric by this ticket. Test-DeploymentAllowlist.ps1 refuses any
target absent from it, and Compare-FabricFolderInventory.ps1 rejects any
post-deployment item that is not declared here.
WHY DATA PATHS ARE HALF OF THIS FILE:
Items live in folders. Lakehouse tables DO NOT. The target folder is an
organisational label, not a boundary - see docs/environment-and-constraints.md.
An item-only allowlist would therefore come back perfectly clean while
someone else's Gold tables were being overwritten. The dataPaths section
is the half that covers the damage the item section cannot see.
Workspace and folder identifiers are deliberately ABSENT. They live in the
gitignored config/environment.local.json because this repository is public.
This file names WHAT may be touched; the local config names WHERE.
$comment_environmentClass: DEPRECATED and retained only so evidence validates against the schema. An
earlier draft of this file recorded 'stable', which contradicted the Issue:
The correction changes no control. The feature/stable distinction was
removed from this repository precisely because it produced ambiguity
without adding a control - see CLAUDE.md rule 5. The real protections are
the target reference, the create-only default and the named-item exception,
and none of them reads this field.
$comment_target: The workspace and folder come from config/environment.local.json only.
requiresExplicitHumanApproval stays true, but NOT because of an environment
class. It is true because deployment requires TWO independent things:
1. the Issue authorising Fabric deployment - Issue #2 does; and
2. a human binding this local target to THIS ticket, by setting
An agent may prepare, plan and evidence the deployment. It may not set that
field. An agent that set its own authorisation flag would be opening its own
gate, which CLAUDE.md rule 12 forbids as plainly as it forbids any other
way of weakening a control to finish a ticket.
$comment_items: createOnly means the deployment script refuses to proceed if the item
already exists with a different definition, rather than overwriting it.
CLAUDE.md forbids overwriting an existing Fabric item; the prefix is what
makes a pre-existing collision unlikely, and the createOnly check is what
catches it when it happens anyway.
$comment_companions: Fabric creates these automatically when a Lakehouse is created. They are
NOT deployed by this ticket and NOT authored in src/, but they will appear
They are declared here so the diff can distinguish 'a documented platform
side effect' from 'an undeclared change', which is the distinction the
diff exists to make. Declaring them is not the same as claiming this
ticket created them - the 'createdBy' field records that honestly.
Note that the SQL analytics endpoint and the default semantic model share
the Lakehouse DISPLAY NAME. That is exactly why the inventory diff keys on

$comment_dataPaths: All paths are relative to the issue2_retail_lakehouse OneLake root and are
scoped to this ticket by the issue2 path segment or the issue2_ table
prefix. No path outside issue2_retail_lakehouse is declared, which means
no path outside it may be written.
Every write is a full overwrite of a ticket-owned path from deterministic
source data. There is no append and no in-place mutation of anything this
ticket did not create, which is what makes a re-run produce the same
result rather than a doubled one.

dataPaths.purpose: Validation audit file written by the run and read back independently over the OneLake DFS endpoint.
Silver - rejected rows with reject reason.

$comment_prohibited: Restating the standing rules at the point of use. These are not new
constraints; they are the ones most likely to be reached for while trying
to make this specific ticket finish.
prohibited: Creating, modifying, renaming or deleting any Fabric item not listed in 'items'.
Writing to any data path not listed in 'dataPaths'.
Deleting or overwriting an item that existed before this ticket.
Creating a workspace, folder or service principal.
Deploying an item whose display name lacks the issue2_ prefix.
Running more than one Fabric job concurrently.
Deploying at all while fabric.authorisedForTicket is not "2".
